captions.detailed: A compact Schmidt-Cassegrain telescope is mounted on a single-arm equatorial fork mount. The stubby, orange cylindrical optical tube assembly features a dark grey front corrector cell and rear cell. It is attached to a single-arm fork that tilts on an angled polar wedge base, supported by a three-legged tripod with thin cylindrical legs. The telescope tube pivots on a declination revolute joint at the tip of the fork arm, while the fork arm itself rotates on a continuous right ascension axis.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a compact Schmidt-Cassegrain telescope on a single-arm equatorial fork mount. The telescope tube should be styled in orange and dark grey, mounted to a single-arm fork that rotates continuously about its polar axis on a tilted wedge plate. Ensure the assembly is supported by a stable three-legged tripod, with revolute joints allowing the telescope to adjust in declination and right ascension.
captions.factory: The design begins by constructing a tripod base consisting of three cylindrical legs angled outward from a central hub. A square wedge plate is mounted on top of the hub, tilted to simulate a polar alignment angle. The single-arm fork is modeled as a rectangular bar offset from a cylindrical base that aligns with the polar axis, creating a continuous revolute joint. The telescope optical tube assembly is built by combining concentric cylinders (representing the orange tube, dark grey cells, and front corrector plate) and is attached via a revolute joint to the tip of the fork arm to allow declination rotation.
